name: eBay used bare A100 40GB SXM4 module (ex-datacenter pull, compliance-gated)
region: United States (seller in Eden Prairie, MN; listing marked US only)
price_basis: USED, BARE SXM4 MODULE with no host server, no baseboard, no heatsink/cooling shroud implied. $2,499.00 = listing 'NVIDIA 699-2G506-0200-310-V A100 40GB SXM4 HBM2 GPU', or Best Offer, captured 2026-10-03. NOTE the record points at the 80GB SXM4 accelerator family id because the repo has no separate A100 40GB record; the part being priced is the 40GB SXM4 variant. Warranty: none from NVIDIA; seller offers 30-day returns, buyer pays return shipping. PRICE CLASS: this is an ASKING price captured from a live listing or product page, i.e. the price at which a seller advertises the part for sale right now. It is NOT a sold/completed transaction price, NOT an auction result and NOT a dealer cost. A realised price on the same day would generally be lower, and for used or refurbished parts the gap between ask and realised is typically wide.
notes:
The most useful anchor in the slice for 'what a single ex-datacenter A100 actually costs'. Seller condition text states it plainly: 'SXM4 Connection. US only. Requires Compliance Approval'. That clause is the norm, not the exception, on used SXM parts - export compliance gating is open and enforced, and a buyer without a compliance path cannot complete the sale. Free FedEx Ground. Seller Core 4 Solutions IT Hardware, 20,700 feedback. Cross-check from the same used-only A100 80GB query (2026-10-03): other bare 40GB SXM4 modules asked $2,499.95 / $2,899.00 / $2,929.99 / $2,999.97 / $3,149.99 / $3,354.99, and used 40GB PCIe cards $6,995-$8,074. So the SXM4 module trades at roughly HALF the used 40GB PCIe price - the form factor, not the silicon, drives the discount, because SXM needs a baseboard. RISK: burn-in and HBM error history are NOT disclosed on any of these listings; the 80GB PCIe listing at $12,500.00 has 'ECC Error' in its own title, which is the honest-disclosure case and rarer than it should be.

EXPORT CONTROL (2026-10-04, mechanism-level; sources spl-eccn-3a090-ccl, spl-bis-2026-01-advanced-computing-case-by-case, spl-bis-2026-05-d5-guidance): these parts classify under ECCN 3A090.a/.b, whose thresholds are 'total processing performance' (TPP) >= 4800, or TPP >= 1600 with performance density >= 5.92 (the .b band is TPP 2400-4800 with performance density 1.6-5.92, or TPP >= 1600 with performance density 3.2-5.92). The mechanism has THREE layers and all three must be cleared, not just one: (a) LICENSE FOR EXPORT FROM THE US - controlled by the January 2026 rule (91 FR 1684, effective 2026-01-15), which moved TPP < 21,000 AND total DRAM bandwidth < 6,500 GB/s parts from presumption of denial to CASE-BY-CASE REVIEW, but only for exports from the US to end users in China/Macau, and only against six exporter certifications - US supply sufficiency judged 'taking into account normal lead times', no diversion of foundry capacity away from US end users, aggregate China+Macau shipments capped at 50% of US end-use shipments, no end-user prohibition, consignee KYC procedures, and prior verification by a qualified third-party US testing lab of TPP, total DRAM bandwidth, interconnect bandwidth and copackaged DRAM capacity; (b) END-USER AND PARENT-COMPANY SCREENING under 742.6(a)(6)(iii)(A) - per BIS guidance of 2026-05-31 a licence is required where the consignee is HEADQUARTERED in Country Group D:5 or Macau OR ITS ULTIMATE PARENT is so headquartered, EVEN IF the consignee itself is outside D:5/Macau, which means the destination country alone never answers the question; (c) THE LIMITS THAT REMAIN - reexports and in-country transfers of the same chips to China/Macau remain PRESUMPTION OF DENIAL, and exports to D:5/Macau-headquartered or -parented entities remain presumption of denial wherever the buyer sits. The Jan-2025 AI Diffusion Rule was rescinded and not enforced from 2025-05-13, but that rescission did not remove (a) or (b).

 LEAD TIME: null, and deliberately so. A secondary-market LISTING has no lead time - the part either exists on the marketplace on the observation date or it does not, and the seller's dispatch time is not published and not a commitment. This is the opposite failure mode from a distributor: a backordered new part at least carries a distribution window (CDW prints '4-6+ Weeks' on some SKUs, source spl-cdw-published-lead-times-gpu-2026-10), whereas a used listing with no buyer carries nothing at all. The correct consequence for a reader is that used and auction supply cannot be scheduled around and therefore cannot carry a build plan - they are opportunistic capacity, which is the strongest argument in this slice for the renting-over-buying decision.
